source.adv: SEC Form ADV Part 1, monthly full files (FOIA frequently-requested documents)
source.market: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)

screen.note: Advisers currently registered with the SEC whose latest Form ADV Part 1 Item 5.F(2)(c) regulatory AUM falls in the band, excluding advisers whose reported private fund gross assets exceed the share limit.

caveats: Regulatory AUM is a prescribed SEC definition. It is not billable assets and not revenue.
One observation per adviser per year, taken from the August full file. Anything that happened inside a year is invisible.

The market-versus-flows split assumes every adviser earned the same blended benchmark. Form ADV Part 1 does not disclose asset allocation, so no per-adviser mix is available. This is the largest single assumption on the site.
Only 16 of 17,018 SEC-registered advisers populate the acquired-firms field, so an absent acquisition flag proves nothing. An acquisition appears in this data as organic growth.
Advisers who fell below the screen, deregistered or were acquired leave the universe, so the surviving set is upward biased.

sources.equity: FRED SP500 (S&P 500 price index), plus a constant dividend add-back
sources.bond: FRED DGS10 (10-year Treasury constant maturity), duration approximation

graduates: Brevan Howard US Investment Management LP
cohort.note: Aggregate flows for the industry are measured on this cohort, not on the index universe. The index universe is defined by the latest filing, which structurally excludes every adviser who outgrew the ceiling and keeps every adviser who shrank into it. The private-fund screen is applied to the cohort using the latest filing; advisers that left the register before the private fund column existed cannot be classified and remain in the cohort.
